title: Act on the Management of Real Estate Development Projects
full_text:
Chapter 1 General Provisions

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to protect the property rights of the people and promote the sound development and stability of the real estate market by providing for basic matters necessary for the management of real estate development projects and the acquisition and utilization of related information, etc. for the systematic development and supply of land, buildings, etc.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act shall be defined as follows:
1. "Real estate development project" means any of the following projects:
(a) A project requiring a building permit for a building under the Building Act with a use and scale prescribed by Presidential Decree (including cases where a building permit under the Building Act is deemed granted under another Act).
(b) A public housing district development project under Article 2, subparagraph 3(a) of the Special Act on Public Housing, a public housing construction project under item (b) of the same subparagraph, or a mixed-use public housing project in an urban center under item (e) of the same subparagraph.
(c) An urban development project under the Urban Development Act.
(d) An improvement project under the Act on the Improvement of Urban Areas and Residential Environments.
(e) A mixed-use development project under the Act on Support for Mixed-Use Development in Urban Centers.
(f) An industrial complex development project under the Industrial Sites and Development Act.
(g) A housing construction project or housing site development project under Article 15 of the Housing Act.
(h) Any other project prescribed by Presidential Decree that is similar to the projects under items (a) through (g).
2. "Project implementer" means a person who implements or intends to implement a real estate development project.
3. "Management of real estate development projects" means systematically collecting and analyzing related information throughout the entire process of real estate development projects and supporting the smooth implementation of such projects.

Article 3 (Basic Principles for the Management of Real Estate Development Projects)
The management of real estate development projects shall conform to the following basic principles:
1. To ensure the efficient use and systematic supply of land, buildings, etc. necessary for the housing and economic activities of the people.
2. To promote the rational use of national land and resources by improving the accessibility and utility of information on real estate development projects.
3. To promote improvement in the quality of people's lives and protect their property rights by ensuring the transparency of information on real estate development projects.
4. To minimize social costs by creating an environment for implementing real estate development projects that responds to social and economic changes.

Article 4 (Relationship to Other Acts)
Except as otherwise specifically provided in other Acts, the management of real estate development projects shall be governed by this Act.

Chapter 2 Management of Real Estate Development Projects

Article 5 (Reporting of Project Plans for Real Estate Development Projects, Etc.)
(1) A project implementer (including a person acting on behalf of a project implementer pursuant to statutes, regulations, and contracts; the same shall apply hereinafter) shall report to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the project plan, financial situation, and financing plan for a real estate development project, within 60 days from the earliest of the following dates:
1. The date on which an agreement is concluded to implement the real estate development project.
2. The date on which land is purchased to implement the real estate development project.
3. The date on which a special purpose corporation or other such entity prescribed by Presidential Decree is established through a capital contribution for the purpose of implementing the real estate development project.
4. The date on which an authorization, permit, etc. for the real estate development project is obtained.
5. Any other date prescribed by Presidential Decree as a date on which implementation of the real estate development project may be regarded as having taken concrete form.
(2) Matters necessary concerning the procedures and methods for reporting under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 6 (Reporting of Cancellation of Real Estate Development Projects, Etc.)
(1) Where a real estate development project reported under Article 5(1) is canceled or suspended for a reason prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the bankruptcy of the project implementer, the project implementer shall report that fact to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport within 60 days from the date on which the real estate development project is canceled or suspended.
(2) The procedures for reporting under paragraph (1) and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 7 (Reporting of Progress of Real Estate Development Projects, Etc.)
(1) A project implementer shall report the progress of a real estate development project reported under Article 5(1) to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) A project implementer shall report the completion of construction of a real estate development project reported under Article 5(1) to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport within 60 days from the date on which construction is completed, such as by obtaining approval for use or undergoing a completion inspection under relevant statutes and regulations.
(3) The procedures for reporting under paragraphs (1) and (2) and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 8 (Verification of Reported Information, Etc.)
(1) Where deemed necessary to verify information reported by a project implementer pursuant to Articles 5 through 7, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may require the project implementer to submit necessary data, have relevant public officials enter the site or facilities of the real estate development project to inspect the current status and other matters relating to the project or examine relevant documents, and have them ask persons concerned necessary questions.
(2) A public official entering a site or facility, conducting an inspection, examining documents, or asking questions under paragraph (1) shall carry identification indicating their authority and present it to the persons concerned.
(3) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport deems cooperation from a relevant institution necessary in connection with verification, inspection, etc. under paragraph (1), the Minister may notify the head of the relevant institution of the facts and request the submission of relevant data or the taking of necessary measures.
(4) The head of a relevant institution who receives a request under paragraph (3) shall notify the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport of the results of the measures taken.

Article 9 (Project Feasibility Assessment, Etc.)
(1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may establish and publicly notify criteria, procedures, methods, etc. for project feasibility assessments of real estate development projects to promote the sound implementation of real estate development projects.
(2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may designate an assessment institution that professionally performs project feasibility assessments and other such work for real estate development projects (hereinafter referred to as an "assessment institution") and publicly notify the designation.
(3) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may revoke the designation of an assessment institution where a reason prescribed by Presidential Decree exists, such as conducting an assessment by improper means, and other matters necessary for the designation, revocation of designation, operation, etc. of assessment institutions shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 10 (Comprehensive Management of Data Relating to Real Estate Development Projects, Etc.)
(1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall comprehensively manage data concerning the project plans, progress, etc. of real estate development projects for the appropriate management and supervision of real estate development projects and the establishment and implementation of related policies, and may provide such data to relevant institutions, organizations, etc. However, information prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as matters concerning managerial or business secrets of a corporation, organization, or individual (hereinafter referred to as "corporations, etc.") that are deemed to pose a risk of substantial harm to the legitimate interests of corporations, etc. if disclosed, shall not be provided.
(2) Where necessary for the management of data under paragraph (1), the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may request the head of a relevant institution to submit data. In such cases, the head of the relevant institution shall comply with the request unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 11 (Establishment and Operation of an Information System for Real Estate Development Projects)
The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may establish and operate an information system for reporting and submitting data concerning real estate development projects, producing relevant statistics, and other such purposes, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to ensure the efficient management of real estate development projects and the stability of the national economy.

Chapter 3 Mediation of Real Estate Development Projects

Article 12 (Establishment of the Mediation Committee, Etc.)
(1) A Real Estate Development Project Mediation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Mediation Committee") shall be established under the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to deliberate on and mediate the following matters concerning real estate development projects for which applications for mediation have been received under Article 17(1):
1. Matters concerning the content of real estate development projects, including project plans;
2. Matters necessary for follow-up management of mediation proposals under Article 20(1);
3. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree for the smooth progress of real estate development projects.
(2) The Mediation Committee shall continue in existence for five years from the date this Act enters into force.

Article 13 (Composition of the Mediation Committee, Etc.)
(1) The Mediation Committee shall consist of not more than 20 members, including one chairperson.
(2) The Vice Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport designated by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall serve as chairperson of the Mediation Committee.
(3) Where the chairperson is unable to perform duties for unavoidable reasons, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act in the chairperson's place.
(4) Members of the Mediation Committee shall be appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport from among the following persons. In such cases, persons who are not public officials shall constitute a majority of the members.
1. Public officials belonging to the Senior Civil Service of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and the Financial Services Commission;
2. Experts with extensive knowledge and experience in real estate, urban planning, architecture, finance, accounting, law, and other relevant fields.
(5) The Mediation Committee shall have one executive secretary to handle its administrative affairs, who shall be a public official belonging to the Senior Civil Service designated by the chairperson.
(6) The term of office of a member who is not a public official shall be two years, and the member may be reappointed for only one consecutive term. However, a member may be removed if the member is unable to perform duties for at least six months owing to illness or other reasons, or has committed misconduct related to those duties.
(7) The term of office of a newly commissioned member replacing a member who is not a public official owing to resignation or other reasons shall be the remainder of the predecessor's term.
(8) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Mediation Committee, the exclusion, challenge, and voluntary recusal of members, and other relevant matters, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (7), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 14 (Disqualifications of Members)
No person falling under any of the following subparagraphs may serve as a member of the Mediation Committee:
1. A person under adult guardianship or limited guardianship;
2. A person who has been declared bankrupt and has not been reinstated;
3. A person who has received an unsuspended sentence of imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment and for whom two years have not elapsed since completion of the execution of that sentence (including cases in which execution is deemed completed) or exemption from its execution;
4. A person who has received a suspended sentence of imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment and is within the period of suspension;
5. A person whose qualifications have been forfeited or suspended pursuant to a court judgment or law.

Article 15 (Meetings of the Mediation Committee)
(1) Meetings of the Mediation Committee shall be convened by the chairperson.
(2) A majority of the members in office shall constitute a quorum for meetings of the Mediation Committee, and resolutions shall be adopted by the affirmative vote of at least two thirds of the members present.
(3) In unavoidable circumstances, the Mediation Committee may adopt resolutions in writing.

Article 16 (Working Committee)
(1) A working committee may be established within the Mediation Committee for the efficient operation of the Mediation Committee.
(2) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the working committee and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 17 (Applications for Mediation, Etc.)
(1) The project implementer of any of the following real estate development projects, or an equity investor in a project under subparagraph 2 or 4, may apply to the Mediation Committee for mediation of the matters set out in the subparagraphs of Article 12(1):
1. A real estate development project implemented by any of the following entities (hereinafter referred to as "public institutions, etc."), including a project implemented jointly with a person other than public institutions, etc.:
(a) The State and local governments;
(b) Public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
(c) Local public corporations and local public agencies under the Local Public Enterprises Act;
2. A real estate development project implemented through a special purpose corporation or similar entity prescribed by Presidential Decree that is established by public institutions, etc. through equity contributions for real estate development, including joint equity contributions with persons other than public institutions, etc.;
3. A real estate development project implemented by a project implementer supplied with land developed by public institutions, etc.;
4. Other real estate development projects for which the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport deems mediation necessary for smooth implementation in connection with authorizations, permits, and other approvals for real estate development projects.
(2) A person who intends to apply for mediation under paragraph (1) shall submit to the Mediation Committee a mediation application form prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, accompanied by documents prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Upon receiving an application for mediation under paragraph (1), the Mediation Committee shall notify the other party of the content of the application without delay. In such cases, the other party receiving the notice shall submit an opinion on the content of the application within 14 days from the date of receipt of the notice.

Article 18 (Dismissal of Applications, Etc.)
(1) The Mediation Committee may dismiss an application for mediation in any of the following cases:
1. Where mediation has been requested on grounds unrelated to the real estate development project subject to mediation by the Mediation Committee;
2. Where a court action has already been brought concerning the matter for which mediation is sought;
3. Where mediation is requested again concerning a matter already undergoing mediation by the Mediation Committee;
4. Where an application for mediation with the same purport as the application for mediation has been filed under other statutes and regulations;
5. Where mediation by the Mediation Committee is deemed inappropriate, or the application for mediation is deemed to have been made for an improper purpose.
(2) Where the Mediation Committee dismisses an application for mediation under paragraph (1), it shall, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, notify the person who applied for mediation under Article 17(1) and the other party notified under the first sentence of paragraph (3) of that Article (hereinafter referred to as the "parties") of that fact.

Article 19 (Mediation Procedures, Etc.)
(1) Upon receiving an application for mediation under Article 17(1), the Mediation Committee shall commence mediation procedures as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Where necessary to prepare a mediation proposal, the Mediation Committee may request each party and interested persons to attend a meeting of the Mediation Committee or submit materials.
(3) Before preparing a mediation proposal, the Mediation Committee shall give each party an opportunity to state opinions orally or in writing (including electronic documents), and may hear the opinions of relevant experts where necessary.
(4) Before preparing a mediation proposal, the Mediation Committee may request the head of the relevant administrative agency having jurisdiction over the real estate development project to submit opinions concerning the mediation proposal. In such cases, the head of the relevant administrative agency receiving the request shall submit opinions within 30 days from the date of receipt of the request.
(5) The Mediation Committee shall terminate mediation procedures and notify each party of that fact in any of the following cases:
1. Where mediation has been concluded, such as where each party agrees to the mediation proposal or the parties resolve the matter themselves;
2. Where mediation has failed because one or both parties do not agree to the mediation proposal;
3. Where there is no longer any practical benefit in continuing the mediation procedures;
4. Where any of the grounds under the subparagraphs of Article 18(1) arises during the mediation procedures.
(6) Matters necessary for mediation procedures, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20 (Presentation of Mediation Proposals, Etc.)
(1) The Mediation Committee shall prepare a mediation proposal containing the following matters and present it to each party:
1. The name, location, and area of the real estate development project subject to mediation;
2. The scope, methods, conditions, and contents of mediation concerning the real estate development project subject to mediation;
3. Matters under Article 12 (1) 2 and 3;
4. Other matters determined by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
(2) Where necessary to prepare a mediation proposal, the Mediation Committee may request specialized institutions, etc. to review the mediation proposal and provide advice thereon.
(3) Each party presented with a mediation proposal pursuant to paragraph (1) shall notify the Mediation Committee whether they agree to it within 60 days from the date it is presented. In such cases, if no response is given as to whether the party agrees, the party shall be deemed to have agreed to the mediation proposal.
(4) Where each party agrees to the mediation proposal pursuant to the first sentence of paragraph (3) (including agreement to a mediation proposal partially revised through consultation among the parties within the period specified in the first sentence of that paragraph; hereinafter the same shall apply in paragraph (5)), or is deemed to have agreed pursuant to the second sentence of paragraph (3), the Mediation Committee shall prepare a written mediation record without delay, and the chairperson and each party shall sign it or affix their names and seals thereto: Provided, That, where the parties are deemed to have agreed pursuant to the second sentence of paragraph (3), the parties' signatures or names and seals may be omitted.
(5) Where a party agrees or is deemed to have agreed to a mediation proposal pursuant to paragraph (3), an agreement with the same contents as the written mediation record under paragraph (4) shall be deemed to have been concluded.

Article 21 (Implementation of Mediation Results and Reporting of Implementation Status)
(1) Each party to a real estate development project for which mediation has been concluded shall faithfully implement the mediation results finalized pursuant to Article 20 (5), and the heads of the relevant administrative agencies having jurisdiction over the real estate development project shall actively cooperate in the work necessary to implement the mediation results.
(2) Where a public official, officer, or employee of public institutions, etc. proactively performs duties to implement mediation results finalized pursuant to Article 20 (5), and their conduct involves no willful misconduct or gross negligence, they shall not be held accountable for the results, including through a request for disciplinary action or reprimand, pursuant to Article 34-3 of the Board of Audit and Inspection Act and Article 23-2 of the Act on Public Sector Audits.
(3) A party who has signed or affixed their name and seal to the Mediation Committee's written mediation record shall periodically report the status of implementation of the mediation results to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 22 (Confidentiality of Mediation Proceedings, Etc.)
The Mediation Committee's mediation proceedings shall not be open to the public: Provided, That they may be made public with the approval of a majority of the Mediation Committee's members.

CHAPTER 4 SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 23 (Entrustment of Duties)
(1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may entrust the following duties to institutions with expertise in the acquisition and management of real estate information and the mediation of real estate development projects, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Receipt of reports on real estate development project plans, etc. under Article 5 (1);
2. Receipt of reports on the cancellation, etc. of real estate development projects under Article 6 (1);
3. Receipt of reports on the progress and completion of construction of real estate development projects under Article 7 (1) and (2);
4. Verification, etc. of the contents of reports under Article 8 (limited to cases where necessary for handling entrusted affairs);
5. Establishment and operation of the real estate development project information system under Article 11;
6. Operation of the Mediation Committee and handling of its affairs;
7. Other duties prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may provide institutions entrusted with duties pursuant to paragraph (1) with financial assistance for all or part of the expenses incurred in performing those duties.

Article 24 (Deeming Persons Public Officials for Purposes of Applying Penalty Provisions)
The following persons shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying Article 127 and Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act:
1. Members of the Mediation Committee who are not public officials;
2. Persons engaged in duties entrusted pursuant to Article 23 (1).

CHAPTER 5 PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 25 (Administrative Fines)
(1) A person falling under either of the following subparagraphs shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won:
1. A person who fails to report a real estate development project plan, etc. or makes a false report in violation of Article 5 (1);
2. A person who fails to report the progress of a real estate development project or makes a false report in violation of Article 7 (1).
(2) A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding three million won:
1. A person who fails to report the cancellation or suspension of a real estate development project or makes a false report in violation of Article 6 (1);
2. A person who fails to report the completion of construction of a real estate development project or makes a false report in violation of Article 7 (2);
3. A person who fails to comply with a request to submit materials; refuses, obstructs, or evades an inspection, examination of records, or questioning; or gives a false response, in violation of Article 8 (1).
(3) The administrative fines under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 20977, May 27, 2025>

Article 1 (Effective Date)
This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation: Provided, That the matters specified in the following subparagraphs shall enter into force on the dates specified therein:

1. Article 9: One year after the date of promulgation;

2. Articles 5 through 8, subparagraphs 1 through 4 of Article 23 (1), and Article 25: Two years after the date of promulgation.

Article 2 (Applicability to Reports on Real Estate Development Project Plans, Etc.)
Articles 5 through 8 shall apply beginning with cases in which the earliest of the dates specified in the subparagraphs of Article 5 (1) occurs after those provisions enter into force.
